conviction_note: Abs move 4.0 is set from the Unusual Whales implied move (+/-4.45%) and the name's fat left tail (-9.4% in Q3 2025, -3.0% in Q2 2026). p_up is 45: the countercyclical fee lines (fixed income, mortgage warehouse) and deposit pricing lean negative, and they are partly offset by a rate path that is kinder to NII than the company's own guide assumed and by buybacks at lower prices. The findings sum to -0.7 against -0.4 scaled. The two agree in sign; the sum is larger because each proxy finding carries its own full small size.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.53 and revenue ~$890M. Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/FHN) shows $0.53 / $889.7M. Benzinga snapshots (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FHN/earnings-forecasts, via search) show $0.52-0.53 / $890.9-893.2M. Two sources agree within a cent. Company FY2026 guide (Q2 slides, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q26earningsslides.htm): adjusted revenue ex deferred comp +3-7% on a $3.42B 2025 base, i.e. $3.52-3.66B; expenses ex deferred comp flat on $2.05B; NIM mid-to-high 340s; NCO 15-25bp; CET1 ~10.5%. 1H26 revenue ex deferred comp was ~$1.743B ($868M + $875M), so 2H26 needs ~$889-958M a quarter. Consensus ~$890M sits at the BOTTOM of the guided range.
positioning_check: Short interest 13.54m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~2.9% of 473.8m outstanding, 2.65 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/fhn/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 via the sweep row). Not crowded. Baseline 25d skew +1.28 vol points, essentially balanced. The front-expiry chain is unusable (ATM spread 100% of mid). Unusual Whales gives an implied earnings move of +/-4.45%, data as of 2026-10-14 (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/FHN/earnings). Tape: -6.2% over 20d, -2.3% over 5d, 14.4% below the 52w high; Earnings Whispers shows -8.2% drift since the 2026-07-15 print. Millennium Management disclosed 5.6% on a 13G (event date 2026-09-28, filed 2026-10-05). As a multi-strategy holder that position is probably hedged.

findings.finding: The rate path is better for NII than FHN's own 2026 guide assumed. The guide's base case (forward curve as of 2025-10-31) assumed 25bp Fed cuts in April and July 2026. Neither happened: the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% in July and hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and the September SEP median implies one more hike. FHN discloses itself as modestly asset sensitive: +2.9% next-12-month NII for +100bp, -3.3% for -100bp (58% variable-rate loans). Against the plan the gap is ~75bp of short rate, worth roughly +2% on ~$2.7B of annual NII. That supports NII and the NIM guide and could raise the FY NII/revenue view on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-15): NIM fell 3bp to 3.49% on deposit costs while EPS beat by a cent; stock -3.03%. FHN has not been paid for NII strength recently; 2 of 7 prints rose.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, but the stock is down 6% over 20 days and 14% off its high in a sector sold on long-rate fears (Beinsure 2026-10-11 preview). If the market had priced the short-rate tailwind to an asset-sensitive bank, FHN would have held up better than the long-rate sell-off. Consensus revenue still sits at the bottom of the guided range rather than moving up.
findings.independence: The Fed action is from a different source: rate tracker / prediction-market pages via search, 'Hike +25 bp, Wednesday, September 16, 2026, Target range 3.75-4.00%' (https://www.noradarealestate.com/?p=83641). A caveat that the finding is sized net of: Zacks noted the mid-September hike has little effect on Q3 itself, so this mostly bears on Q4 and the guide. The asset side only; finding 4 is the funding side of the same NIM line.

findings.finding: FHN Financial fixed income, the countercyclical fee line, is likely to fall again in Q3. Its own ADR fell from $771k (3Q25) to $765k, $742k and $594k (2Q26), and fixed income revenue from $57M to $46M. Since then, Wells Fargo's Q3 2026 FICC revenue fell 18% q/q ($1,536M to $1,262M, release 2026-10-13). Regions told investors in Aug-Sep that Q3 capital-markets fees would trend to the low end of $90-105M 'amid market volatility and elevated rates'. FHN's CEO described a rate backup 'accelerating in Q3' (Barclays, 2026-09-15). A 10-20% q/q drop is $5-9M of revenue, ~0.6-1.0% of the ~$890M bar, partly offset by lower commissions/incentives.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Countercyclical revenue drives FHN's revenue guide range (3-7%). In Q2 2026 fixed income fell $7M q/q and the stock fell 3.03% on a 1c EPS beat. In Q3 2025 a cost miss on incentive-heavy expenses sent it -9.43%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue (~$890M, roughly flat on Q2's $887-890M) does not visibly embed another q/q fee decline. A priced fee drop would show as consensus below Q2 revenue, given NII growth is only ~$9M a quarter. The WFC FICC print is two days old, so the FHN consensus is unlikely to have moved on it.
findings.independence: FHN ADR trend: Q2 slides (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q26earningsslides.htm). Regions' capital-markets guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000057/a3q26investormeetingmate.htm. These are proxies: FHN Financial is a rates-distribution business to depository institutions, not FICC trading. Net of the rest: lower countercyclical revenue lowers incentive expense, which the guide explicitly excludes.

findings.finding: FHN's CEO said at Barclays on 2026-09-15 that mortgage warehouse lending (loans to mortgage companies) had 'softened due to higher rates'. LMC was a growth engine: average balances $4.28B in 2Q26, +10% q/q and +21% y/y, ~7% of loans. Rising long rates also hit mortgage banking fees: FB Financial, a Nashville footprint peer, reported Q3 2026 mortgage banking income -16% q/q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history isolating LMC. Loan growth was cited as the positive in Q2 2026 and the stock still fell 3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The comment was a conference remark summarised by a third party, not a guidance change. If priced, loan-growth estimates and the balance-sheet growth view would have been trimmed in previews. None found.
findings.independence: FB Financial Q3 2026 8-K, mortgage banking $11.2M to $9.4M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm, 2026-10-13). The Quartr summary is AI-generated, secondary and snippet-level. Net of the rest: C&I ex-LMC grew $710M in Q2 and the CEO called pipelines strong, so total loan growth may hold.

findings.finding: Deposit costs are rising into Q3. Q2 interest-bearing deposit cost averaged 2.33% with a quarter-end spot of ~2.43%, and management guided deposit costs to 'trend up slightly'. On 2026-09-15 the CEO said Q3 deposit growth was strong 'supported by incentives'. FB Financial, a Nashville footprint peer, reported Q3 2026 NIM -12bp (3.95% to 3.83%) and interest-bearing deposit cost +7bp, citing increased deposit pricing. A similar 5-10bp rise on FHN's ~$52B interest-bearing deposits is $6-13M a quarter and would push NIM toward or below the bottom of the 'mid to high 340s' guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: NIM -3bp on brokered-deposit cost while EPS beat; stock -3.03%. NIM and expense quality, not EPS, have driven FHN's reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 spot rate of 2.43% against the 2.33% average is in the release but not in headline consensus. If priced, consensus NII would be flat rather than growing and Q3 EPS would have been cut from $0.53. It was not (Earnings Whispers $0.53).
findings.independence: FHN's own Q2 release spot rate (https://s21.q4cdn.com/903615748/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/2Q2026-Earnings-Release.pdf) and the CEO's Barclays remark (Quartr). Different documents, same direction. Offsets: finding 1 (the asset side benefits from the hike), and Regions guided Q3 NIM stable to higher with stable deposit costs, though Regions is rate-neutral with a lower-cost deposit base.

findings.finding: Millennium Management crossed 5% of FHN: 23.5m shares on 2026-09-01 (dipped back below 5% by the 2026-09-09 filing), then 26.3m shares, 5.6%, event date 2026-09-28, 13G filed 2026-10-05. A large multi-strategy holder building into the print, most likely hedged pod or market-making inventory rather than a directional bet.
findings.why_not_priced: 13G passive filings from multi-strats are rarely covered. If the market read it as an M&A signal, the stock would not be at -6% over 20d.
findings.independence: Earlier 13G: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/36966/000110465926106405/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml (4.97% after crossing 5% on 2026-09-01). Same filer, so not independent.

findings.finding: Buybacks are likely to be stepped up at lower prices. $665M remains under the authorization; Q2 bought $100M at $24.52; the stock is now $22.46, ~8% lower. Diluted shares fell from 510m (3Q25) to 480m (2Q26), and period-end shares were 474m at 2Q26. Another ~$100-150M at ~$23.5 retires ~4-6m shares and lifts EPS ~0.5-1%. CET1 is 10.5%, at target, which limits the pace unless loan growth slows (and LMC softening frees capital).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks were continuous through 2025-26; no print reaction attributable to them.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS is unchanged at $0.53 while the share price fell; a priced acceleration would show as EPS estimates edging up. Small, because it lands inside the CET1 target the company already guided.
findings.independence: Q2 release share data (https://s21.q4cdn.com/903615748/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/2Q2026-Earnings-Release.pdf). Same company, so not independent.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (+1.28) and the chain unusable. The negative lean on fees and deposit costs agrees with the -6% 20-day run-up, so part of it may already be in the price. That is why p_up sits at 45, not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy) and lesson 9 (net of the rest): fixed income cut from -0.9 to -0.6. The WFC FICC and Regions reads are proxies, and lower countercyclical revenue also lowers incentive expense.
Lesson 9: LMC/mortgage cut from -0.4 to -0.3, because LMC is ~7% of loans and C&I ex-LMC and pipelines were strong.
Lesson 3: checked that the rate-path (+0.5) and deposit-cost (-0.7) findings can both be true (asset side vs funding side). Kept separate, cross-referenced in independence.
Lessons 1 and 7: the name sells beats and short interest is not crowded. The scaled p_up of 45 and abs_move of 4.0 are unchanged.
